title: GSoC, LFX & Outreachy: Mentorship Roadmap
subtitle: Pick an org, draft the proposal, write the mentor note.
description: Skip the ‘what is GSoC’ overview. This week you choose a program, shortlist issues, and write a proposal a mentor could mark up — using the official student guide plus accepted-proposal habits.
outcomes: Mentorship application drafted — org pick, proposal, mentor note

modules.title: Apply like a contributor, not a tourist
modules.summary: How people actually get in: org pick, contributions, proposal, mentor message.

lessons.title: How I got into GSoC: org pick, contributions, proposal
lessons.description: A contributor walkthrough: start on page two of the org list, write up your local setup as a first patch, stay on one org, and put a week-by-week timeline plus research in the proposal.

lessons.title: Nail your GSoC proposal (what mentors actually mark)
lessons.description: OpenMRS mentors on the template they use, the sections they skip, and why a messy draft sent early beats a perfect PDF at 23:59. Pair with https://google.github.io/gsocguides/student/writing-a-proposal

lessons.title: LFX Mentorship: how the board and terms work
lessons.description: Linux Foundation mentorships: terms, CNCF/kernel-adjacent projects, and how you apply on the LFX board (up to a few tailored projects per term).

lessons.title: Outreachy: initial application, then the contribution period
lessons.description: How the Outreachy initial application is structured and what the contribution period is for. Read the current applicant guide before you write: https://www.outreachy.org/docs/applicant/

lessons.title: Studio: Org shortlist + proposal draft
lessons.description: Pick one program and one org. List three issues. Write a 12-week proposal a mentor could comment on. Draft the first chat message.

assignment.brief: Use this year’s official pages — dates move. GSoC: https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/ and the student proposal guide. LFX: https://mentorship.lfx.linuxfoundation.org/. Outreachy: https://www.outreachy.org/docs/applicant/. Depth on one org beats spraying twenty.
assignment.deliverable: A mentor-facing proposal draft, not an essay about your passion.

fields.label: Program + organization + why this pair
fields.placeholder: GSoC / LFX / Outreachy — org name — I can set this up locally because…
fields.hint: Name a language or repo you can compile this week. ‘Prestige org’ is not a reason.

fields.label: Three issues or idea-list items you would take first
fields.placeholder:
1. URL — what it asks — first file you would open
2. …
3. …
fields.hint: Real URLs. Include at least one you could finish before the application deadline.

fields.label: Proposal draft: problem, approach, 12-week timeline
fields.placeholder:
Problem the org has…
What I will ship (required vs optional)…
Weeks 1–4 / 5–8 / 9–12…
Risks and fallback…
fields.hint: Follow the official sections: https://google.github.io/gsocguides/student/writing-a-proposal — deliverables a mentor can check, not vibes.

fields.label: First message to a mentor (chat or email)
fields.placeholder: Hi — I built the project locally (blocked on X, fixed by Y). I read issue #… and I would start by … Does that match what you want?
fields.hint: Show setup + a specific issue. Do not send ‘please tell me how to start’ with no repo clone.

checklist: You named one program and one org, not five.
The timeline has weeks and deliverables, including a fallback.
The mentor note proves you ran the project locally.

lessons.title: Assessment: Mentorship Programs
lessons.description: Pick the right program — and the work that has to happen before the form.

questions.prompt: The strongest GSoC / LFX / Outreachy application usually includes:

options.text: Zero prior PRs and a very long essay.
Merged (or at least serious) contributions to the org, plus a specific proposal.
A promise to learn the language after selection only.
Copy-pasting last year's winning proposal unchanged.

questions.explanation: Mentors pick people they have already seen in the issue tracker. Proof of work beats a generic essay.

options.text: Outreachy is only for people who already completed GSoC.
LFX Mentorship is run around Linux Foundation / CNCF-style projects in seasonal terms.
GSoC still requires you to be enrolled in a university.
All three programs merge your PRs without a mentor.

questions.explanation: LFX is the LF/CNCF mentorship board. GSoC has not required student status since 2022. Outreachy has its own eligibility (underrepresented in tech) and a contribution phase. Always read the current year's rules.

options.text: Read this year's official timeline; dates move.
Pick 1–2 orgs and show up in their chat/issues early.
You can skip CONTRIBUTING.md if the stipend is large.
A proposal should name a project, a mentor-facing plan, and a realistic schedule.

questions.explanation: Timelines change. Depth beats spraying 20 orgs. Proposals are project plans, not vibes. Process docs still apply.
